criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical headings and executive summary present, but figures lack numbers/titles, tables poorly formatted, grammar errors, malformed refs, and prohibited Wikipedia used as design source.

technical_issues.issue: Semi-major axis 7171 km for 600 km altitude wrong; should be 6971 km. Inclination 87.79 deg not SSO retrograde; plot shows ~97.8 deg, text contradicts retrograde claim.
Kourou latitude quoted as 45.05 N; actual ~5.2 N. RAAN 27.33 deg justified as launch facility location is incorrect.
Mean access 580.8 s (~9.7 min), max 770 s (~12.8 min), so claim of almost twenty minutes average is false, overstating link by ~2x.

overall: Single-satellite GBR fluid-lensing mission with full segment coverage and STK evidence, but marred by orbit calculation errors, vague operations, poor referencing and missing design files.

feedback.summary: You proposed a well-motivated single-satellite GBR fluid-lensing mission with good STK coverage of launch, orbit and ground contacts. To reach Accomplished you need to fix orbit maths, clarify operator/customers and operations, and improve presentation, referencing and evidence files.
next_steps: Recalculate and correct your Orbit semi-major axis to 6971 km, reconcile 87.79 deg vs 97.8 deg in Image 4 for true retrograde SSO, and fix Kourou latitude and RAAN justification in your Launch section.

Clarify in your Introduction operator versus customers and in Ground Control & Communications use your access table mean 580.8 s and max 770 s to justify realistic contact frequency, not almost twenty minutes.
Number and title all your figures including Image 4, tidy tables, replace Wikipedia in your Bibliography with primary sources, and attach your STK files to strengthen evidence.

criteria.C1: You described well in Introduction your fluid-lensing GBR mission need and why 'only one satellite is required' for scientists to predict bleaching. For Accomplished, explicitly name operator versus customers instead of vague Australia facilities and implied scientists, with literature support.
criteria.C2: You covered in Launch, Orbit and Ground Control & Communications your Vega E choice, orbit elements with STK views, ground-tracks and access table. For Accomplished, correct 7171 km to 6971 km, resolve 87.79 deg vs 97.8 deg retrograde in Image 4, fix Kourou 45.05 N and RAAN, correct ~20 min claim vs 580.8 s mean, and include STK files.
criteria.C3: You recapped in Conclusion launch, polar sun-synchronous orbit for 'consistent illumination of the oceans' and bleaching benefit. For Accomplished, expand beyond brief generic summary to detailed conclusions fully tied to evidence, addressing Vega E uncertainty implications.
criteria.C4: You used logical headings and executive summary, which aids readability. For Accomplished, number/title figures including Image 4, format tables consistently, proofread grammar, fix malformed Bibliography entries and replace Wikipedia e.g. 2021_in_spaceflight with proper sources cited correctly.
